sentences.text: Two species of Graculavus are known: G. augustus from the Western Interior Seaway and G. velox from the Atlantic Seaboard.
The genus Graculavus was described by O. C. Marsh in 1872.
Fossils of Graculavus have been found in the Austin Chalk of Texas, the Lance Formation, and the Hornerstown Formation.
Graculavus is the namesake for the form taxon Graculavidae, which was historically considered a group of transitional shorebirds.
Graculavus belongs to the parent group Charadriiformes.
The species formerly known as Graculavus lentus is now considered an early galliform or close relative placed in the genus Austinornis.
Graculavus lived on the shores of the northwestern Atlantic and the Western Interior Seaway approximately 68 million years ago.
Graculavus lived from the Maastrichtian to the Danian stages, between 72.2 and 61.66 million years ago.
